name: Devin 2.0 (Cognition)
description: Per-session isolated VM, machine snapshots as workspace-state primitive, parallel managed Devins, teamspace isolation. Discards uncommitted work at session end. Strong reference for snapshot/restore semantics.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Account-based and required. Users sign in to a Cognition/Devin cloud account (app.devin.ai). Enterprise deployments support org SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, and generic SAML/OIDC providers). Identity governs seat/usage, workspace access, persisted secrets, and connected integrations (GitHub, Slack). For headless/automation, an API key authenticates programmatic session creation. [uncertain]
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Designed for teams and orgs. Team plan provides shared usage; Enterprise adds VPC deployment, SAML/OIDC SSO, centralized admin controls, consolidated billing/usage analytics across multiple Devin organizations, and explicit teamspace isolation that separates departments/teams. Multiple developers share connected repos and can each run their own (and managed) Devins. Collaboration is asynchronous/oversight-style — humans steer and review via session links, Slack, and PRs — rather than co-editing one live agent buffer. [uncertain]

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A workspace is a managed, account-scoped cloud entity (configured at app.devin.ai/workspace), not merely a local directory. It is realized as a saved machine state (a machine snapshot) that bundles one or more connected repositories plus the installed environment (tools, dependencies, env). By default every session boots a fresh copy of this snapshot containing all repositories added to the workspace. So the workspace is virtual/cloud-defined and maps to a snapshot image rather than 1:1 to a single git repo or a fixed filesystem path; multiple repos can co-exist in one snapshot, and advanced users can maintain multiple distinct machine snapshots to start sessions from different saved states.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Each session is bound to a workspace/snapshot and runs in its own isolated VM (Devbox). At session start, the workspace resets to the saved machine state and the latest code is pulled for the relevant repo(s). A user (and a team) can run many sessions concurrently against the same workspace, each in its own isolated VM with its own terminal/browser/IDE and its own session link. Sessions are independent; they do not share live filesystem state with each other (isolation by VM), only the common starting snapshot.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Session-level: the isolated VM filesystem, terminal/browser state, and the interactive plan for that task — all discarded at session end. Workspace-level: the machine snapshot (repos + environment), Blueprints (declarative env config), persisted secrets and site cookies (usable across all future sessions), Devin Wiki/Search index, and Playbooks/Knowledge. Org/teamspace-level: admin policy, SSO, and teamspace isolation boundaries. Knowledge and Playbooks provide durable, reusable context layered on top of the per-session VM.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Environment is configured declaratively via YAML Blueprints, which Devin can auto-generate by analyzing the project (user reviews/approves); Blueprint builds run to produce the snapshots every session boots from. Maintenance/setup commands are surfaced to the agent as context at session start rather than always auto-executed (the agent may re-run them if it detects dependency drift). For agent behavior/instructions, Devin uses Playbooks and Knowledge plus rule files: it recognizes a .devin/rules directory (preferred, takes precedence) with .windsurf/rules kept as a backward-compatible fallback; rules are discovered in the workspace, sub-directories, and parent dirs up to the git root. (This rules precedence is shared lineage with Windsurf/Codeium under Cognition.) [uncertain]
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not a bounded research-source product. Grounding corpus = the connected repositories in the workspace snapshot, surfaced through Devin Search (agentic codebase Q&A with cited code) and Devin Wiki (auto-generated repo documentation). Retrieval is scoped to the repos present in the active snapshot/workspace rather than to a curated PDF/web/video source set.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Hybrid. Durable workspace/env state is persisted as machine snapshots (saved VM images) plus declarative Blueprints, plus persisted secrets/cookies and Knowledge/Playbooks/Wiki — all stored in Cognition's cloud and tied to the account/workspace. Session conversation/metadata is stored cloud-side and addressable via per-session links and the API. The agent's runtime filesystem is ephemeral VM storage. The primary durable output channel for work product is Git (commits/PRs to connected GitHub repos). Exact backing datastores are not publicly documented. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.session_history: Each session has a persistent session link/page in the cloud (web app) where its transcript, plan, actions, terminal/browser activity, and results can be inspected and where the user can message the running Devin. Sessions are referenceable later via @-mentions to point a new session at prior work. Sessions are accessible via the API for programmatic creation/inspection. Browsable in the web UI; the underlying storage format and explicit retention/export policy are not publicly documented. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Layered durable knowledge separate from ephemeral runtime. Ephemeral: the per-session VM filesystem and in-task plan (wiped at session end). Durable, agent/user-curated: Knowledge (facts/conventions the agent and user accumulate), Playbooks (reusable procedures the agent can create and improve), Devin Wiki (auto-generated repo understanding), and machine snapshots/Blueprints (environment memory). Devin can autonomously create/improve playbooks and manage knowledge. This separates short-term thread state (VM) from long-term cross-session stores (Knowledge/Playbooks/Wiki/snapshots) at the architecture level.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: Devin Search provides agentic semantic search over the codebase (with cited code), and Devin Wiki provides navigable auto-generated docs — both are workspace/repo-scoped. Prior sessions can be retrieved/referenced into a new session via @-mentions rather than via a full-text transcript search UI. No documented global semantic search across all past session transcripts. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Strongly ephemeral session semantics and a key reference for discard-on-end behavior: each session boots a fresh copy of a snapshot, and when the session ends ALL changes are discarded — anything not committed to a repo or captured in a new snapshot disappears. To persist environment changes the user must take a new machine snapshot (e.g. after installing dependencies) or update the Blueprint. Persistent secrets/cookies and Knowledge/Playbooks survive across sessions by design. Non-Git intermediate artifacts (logs, reports, scratch files) must be exported outside the VM to survive. Explicit numeric TTL/retention for session records is not publicly documented. [uncertain]

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: Strong VM-level isolation. Architecture splits into the Brain (stateless cloud inference service, always in Cognition's cloud) and the Devbox (a secure isolated virtual machine where code runs). Each session — and each managed Devin — gets its own isolated VM with its own terminal, browser, and full dev environment, able to run shell commands, execute tests, and self-verify. Enterprise can deploy within a customer VPC for data residency/security. Per-session network policy specifics and resource limits are not publicly detailed. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: Core differentiator. Machine snapshots are first-class save states of the VM's full machine state (filesystem + installed packages/tools + configured environment), saved and restored independently of any conversation. Every session boots from a chosen snapshot; users can maintain multiple snapshots to start from different saved states, and Blueprints declaratively (re)build snapshots. This cleanly separates environment/filesystem state from session/conversation history — the strongest snapshot/restore reference among comparable tools.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Cloud-native, managed execution; there is no documented migration of a running session between cloud and a developer's local machine. There is a Devin Desktop/IDE client experience for interacting with cloud Devins, and Enterprise VPC self-hosting, but execution itself stays in the managed Devbox rather than relocating to local. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: First-class parallel fan-out via Managed Devins. A main Devin session acts as a coordinator: it scopes the task, delegates pieces to multiple managed Devins (each a full Devin in its own isolated VM with its own session link), monitors progress, resolves conflicts, and compiles results. Composes with Scheduled Devins for recurring parallel jobs (e.g. weekly QA across pages, results posted to Slack). Parallel Devins isolate workspace state via separate VMs (each from the snapshot) rather than sharing a live filesystem. Concrete max-parallelism limits are not publicly specified. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Multiple entry points: the web app (app.devin.ai), Slack, and a public API for programmatic/headless session creation; Scheduled Devins add cron-style automated triggers; a desktop/IDE client also exists. Slack and API are emphasized for team workflows and automation. [uncertain]

implementation.implementation_stack: Two-tier cloud architecture: a stateless Brain (model inference) in Cognition's cloud, and isolated Devbox VMs for execution. Auth/identity: Cognition account with enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO; API keys for programmatic access. Workspace/env state: machine snapshots (saved VM images) + declarative YAML Blueprints + persisted secrets/cookies. Durable agent knowledge: Knowledge store, Playbooks, Devin Wiki, and Devin Search (semantic code search/index). Integrations: GitHub (primary output via commits/PRs), Slack, and REST API; Scheduled Devins for cron automation. Underlying databases/queues, snapshot storage backend, and session-record format are not publicly documented. [uncertain]
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Devin is the prime reference for snapshot/restore and discard-on-end semantics that Labmate's execution/isolation layer should emulate conceptually. Map Devin's per-session isolated VM -> a Labmate ephemeral execution/session context whose volatile state lives in Redis Streams with a TTL and is intentionally discarded at session end, while durable outcomes are persisted explicitly (Devin's analogue is Git commits/PRs; Labmate's is MongoDB session docs + any committed artifacts). Adopt Devin's clean separation of environment-state (machine snapshot / Blueprint) from conversation-state (session history): in Labmate terms, keep workspace/environment config as a versioned, restorable artifact distinct from LangGraph thread_id checkpoints so a workspace can be re-instantiated without replaying chat history. Borrow the coordinator + managed-subagent pattern for parallel fan-out (a parent thread spawning child thread_ids, each isolated, results compiled back). Use a stable cloud workspace_id (account-scoped, repo-bundling) rather than a filesystem path for scoping — directly addressing the workspace_id scoping recommendation. For identity, mirror required account auth + org/teamspace isolation (multi-tenant workspace boundaries) as Labmate scales beyond single users. For the Discord connector as a session entry point, model it after Devin's Slack/API trigger surface: a connector that authenticates a user, resolves a workspace_id, and creates a session bound to it. The discard-uncommitted-work rule is the key safety principle: define explicitly in Labmate what survives a session (Mongo-persisted docs/decisions) vs what is dropped (Redis ephemeral working state).
